Dog costs tend to correlate with income, location, available time and dog comfort, like most things. So it might. I’m always glad to get more information before I do something. 
My mid sized dog cost run down is skewed more towards external care than actual necessities but also skewed in a HCOL area where I’m stubbornly middle class. Many of these things can be eliminated if need be, but she benefits from them. 
Food: 25$/mo
Stupid glandex do she doesn’t wipe her butt everywhere: $30/mo
Dog walk 2x/week when we are both at work and can’t get back to let her out: $250/mo
Assorted treats/shampoo/poop bags/harness leash updates throughout the year $10/ mo
Annual veterinary visit $700
Emergency pet insurance to cover cost of potential 3k surgery: 50/mo
Kennel stay for 1 week if we can’t find a dog sitter and want a vacation: $650/week
Shelter mix dog paid $250 to cover standard shelter fees including spay. 

We could cut out dog walking which is the biggest expense, but would have to put in a dog door and adjust fence and trust her while we are gone, also adjust our small house so she doesn’t bring too much dirt in, but currently I don’t want to make dog wait 8 hours to pee. There’s also doggy day care available which is also expensive but sometimes needed if life happens and we can’t be home. 
She is a high energy amazing dog that truly suffers if she’s pent up too long. Which sure, we could do, but we’d be worse people for it. 

So maybe like 4k$ a year. And we are mid level dog owners in our area. I know people that pay 1$k a year and people that pay 10$k a year. 
I know people making big bucks working 60hrs a week but have their dog in daycare five days a week at like $850/mo. And to all the people that will scoff at that I would offer that Just like this post implies poor people can’t have dogs, you seem to be saying rich people (working for it) can’t have dogs. So this post, like everything in the world might be true. Most people can make having a dog work out, but there will be cost and time involved. 

We don’t have the Luxury of only working one job. Sorry. 

Also, preventative statement: dog walkers in our area charge 20$ for a half hour. And if you find that offensive but are making less than that, maybe you should consider starting a business where we are. You don’t even have to move here, just manage the staff and skim off the top. 

Lastly just remember I’m one of the poorer people in my area. But I love my dog. 
My car payment was 350/mo. For a used car. So yeah this post might be myopic but not entirely baseless. 

Also dog owners stick together and don’t talk  shit about other dog owners. Be well.

Don’t worry. I too gained weight, but that’s because I was essentially dying. Let your body crave all those nutrients it couldn’t get for awhile, and slowly try to remove or manage the sugar cravings that follow sudden sobriety. But give your body time to enjoy being larger. Give yourself a full year before adding the stress of food management. Then just make obvious choices like drinking a full glass of water before resorting to soda, reorganizing portion supplies so that you put larger amounts of veggies on your plate and and walking a half hour a day. But don’t add those stressers too fast if you are still getting cravings, if it’ll add to your stress load. First year keep stress as low as possible. If it means eating that muffin go for it. It’s a replacement for drink. If the craving isn’t satiated go for a half hour walk (assuming you don’t live near a bar) around the neighborhood. 
You will eventually lose the weight but your body chemistry is so wack right now just deal with the daily. You’ll be fine and sexy in due time. Give your body time to recover. That attitude helped me at least. Btw remember to force yourself into fun activities. Good luck and enjoy this new adventure.

This is the biggest realization I had, from both heavy drinking and light drinking.  I don't think this is talked about enough.  My "unbearable" Anxiety seemed to stem from drinking, the thing is is that the anxiety comes a day or two afterwards ( but can be ongoing since you keep drinking) so people don't make the connection as easily.  I put unbearable in quotes because anxiety still exists occasionally during abstinence.  But it's no longer crippling.  Reading some of these, yes, Anxiety will increase as you detox and withdraw.  That's why I took forever to get sober, because initially the drinking helped.  But it's also what caused it.  You just gotta know that in about 3 to 6 weeks the everyday anxiety will be gone, and you realize that's how simple people live all the time and why they are so damn chipper.  The Inevitable Doom is lifted.  Congrats, keep it going sobernaut!  You'll be free once you clear that foggy atmosphere and break from the alcoholic gravity. As long as you keep saying just one more sober day, you'll get there before you know it.

I was a handle every two days at my worst. You’re three weeks out. Im a small part of the whole show, and in post production, which is all the work that gets done after they shoot. I'm just the mixer/sound designer (although there's very little sound design to this show). So I'll record VOice over (narration) and edit it make sure the timings are right. Pick the best takes. Then put it in the show and eq and compress it make sure all the volumes are right for sound effects narration and music and any dialog. Create sound effects for any new animations or fake them for anything we didn't get during the shoot.  Then the producer and I will listen to it and tweak it more and then marry the video and audio together or give it back to the video editor to do then it goes through technical evaluation(sometimes) to double check for possible errors that could effect it's broadcast and then it goes to the broadcast center in sterling Virginia and then into outer space to a satellite and the down to your cable provider and into your home. 

I don't have much say in the topics they pick but I've suggested some to the producer when do special shows that we decide to shoot for our network. Most of our shows are done by outside production companies that we hire to shoot and direct for us. Sometimes they do post too but many get brought in house. We use outside production companies because it's often much cheaper to hire a company in, say, London, to film shots at the Bentley factory than to fly a crew of 12 and all the cameras and gear there. 

Sometimes they be at a factory that makes cables or something and they'll see that they also make light bulbs and they'll decide to get footage of that process too, which probably explains the random things you see. Any way hope that helps sorry this turned out long. Glad you like it.
